in_text_mentions: d noted a swelling of the right sterno-clavicular joint. Magnetic resonance imaging showed synovial reaction and intra-articular effusion with bone marrow oedema of the right sterno-clavicular joint (Figure 1). Magnetic resonance is an excellent technique to show cartilaginous, joints and bone abnormalities, therefore it represents the elective method in the investigation of Tietze syndrome. It has been employed in cases of chest wall pain following thoracic trauma, spondyloarthropathies, septic arthritis and malignant tumours that may mimic Tietze syndrome. panels.rationale: Single-panel high-frequency ultrasound of the sternocostal joints in a real patient, explicitly captioned as showing an oval-shaped hypoechoic focus 'typical for Tietze syndrome' at the 4th manubriosternal joint with distortion of the joint contour, matching the article's primary disease (Tietze syndrome) and the chondral enlargement on imaging finding. Red arrow annotation present; no skin, age or ethnicity information available.
panels.attribution_text: Kuridze et al. Tietze Syndrome as a Cause of Chest Pain in the Post-COVID-19 Period.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.37360. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound scan image of the sternocostal joints done during the first visit Ultrasound scan image of the sternocostal joints at the first visit shows an oval-shaped hypoechoic focus which is typical for Tietze syndrome.
in_text_mentions: Considering the patient's complaints, an ultrasound scan of the sternocostal joints was performed using a high-frequency 10 MHz transducer. During the examination, an oval-shaped hypoechoic focus measuring 16mm/8mm/7mm was discovered at the 4th manubriosternal joint, distorting the joint contour (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of the upper chest of a 41-year-old patient from a case report titled 'Tietze Syndrome in a 41-Year-Old Patient Without Significant Comorbidities'. The caption and in-text examination describe visible swelling (with erythema, heat and tenderness) at the right sternoclavicular/costochondral junction, a classic clinical manifestation of Tietze syndrome; the green circle highlights the swelling, so it is annotated but remains a genuine patient image.

A physical examination revealed erythema, heat, and tenderness at the right sternoclavicular junction (Figure 1), along with pain on palpation and limited range of motion in the right arm. During the primary assessment, the patient’s vital signs were within normal limits, with clear airways and normal lung sounds bilaterally.
